protocol.text:
# Protocol — colchicine for prevention of pericarditis recurrence

**Registration.** The commit that adds/updates this file is the registration of this
review; its SHA is embedded in the page's Protocol tab and its Reproducibility tab.
Committed BEFORE the synthesis is run. (Revised from the initial recurrent-only draft
to match the scope of the resolved open-access comparator and to put eligibility on
P/I/C/**design** only — see below.)

## PICO
- **P** — patients with pericarditis (acute first episode or recurrent) treated to prevent recurrence.
- **I** — colchicine added to conventional anti-inflammatory therapy.
- **C** — placebo added to conventional therapy.
- **O (primary)** — recurrent pericarditis during follow-up.
- **O (harms / secondary)** — adverse events, treatment discontinuation, and any further
  outcome the resolved comparator reports.

## Estimand / population / timepoint
- **Estimand** — risk ratio (RR), colchicine vs placebo.
- **Population** — intention-to-treat as randomised.
- **Timepoint** — longest recurrence follow-up each trial reports.

## Eligibility — on P/I/C/DESIGN ONLY
Include a record iff **all** hold:
- **I1** — randomised controlled trial;
- **I2** — population is pericarditis (acute or recurrent), treated to prevent recurrence;
- **I3** — colchicine vs placebo, both added to conventional therapy;
- **design** — double-blind, placebo-controlled.

Exclude (reason must be true of the record):
- **X1** — not an RCT (review, guideline, observational, protocol-only);
- **X2** — wrong population (e.g. postpericardiotomy-syndrome prophylaxis);
- **X3** — wrong intervention/comparison (no colchicine-vs-placebo contrast);
- **X-DESIGN** — not double-blind and placebo-controlled (e.g. open-label);
- **X5** — off-topic: a primary trial of another topic in this set (negative control).

> **Eligibility is NOT on the outcome axis.** Whether a trial reports the recurrence
> outcome, or gives a 2×2 vs only an effect+CI, is recorded as *target-result status* at
> extraction — never as an exclusion. A published effect + 95% CI is a poolable input.

## Search (fetch-once; raw results committed under cache/<slug>/search.json; screening replays offline)
- PubMed: colchicine × pericarditis × (recurrent OR trial); plus meta-analysis sweeps to resolve the comparator.
- ClinicalTrials.gov: condition "recurrent pericarditis", intervention "colchicine".

## Synthesis method (DECLARED; served method must equal this — gate limb 1)
Random-effects inverse-variance on log(RR); **Paule-Mandel** τ²; **HKSJ** 95% CI on
`t_{k-1}` with variance floor `max(1, Q/(k-1))`; prediction interval
`μ ± t_{k-1}·√(τ²+se²)`. 0.5 continuity correction to all four cells of a study only if
it has a zero cell. DerSimonian-Laird forbidden. Engine validated vs metafor 5.0.1 (<1e-6).

## Comparator (resolved; open-access confirmed)
Imazio et al., *Heart* 2012, "Efficacy and safety of colchicine for pericarditis
prevention" (PMID 22442198, DOI 10.1136/heartjnl-2011-301306; Unpaywall is_oa=true). It
reports pooled recurrence RR 0.40 (0.30–0.54) over 5 controlled trials plus adverse
events and drug-withdrawal. Trial-set overlap is stated on the page.

## Controls
- **Positive** — the search must recover the canonical double-blind colchicine-vs-placebo
  pericarditis RCTs (CORP, CORP-2, ICAP).
- **Negative** — COLCOT (colchicine, double-blind, placebo-controlled, but post-MI coronary
  disease — another topic in this set) must be recovered and EXCLUDED (X5).

sources.name: PubMed
queries: colchicine AND pericarditis AND (recurrent OR recurrence) AND (randomized OR randomised OR trial)  -> 148 hits
colchicine pericarditis (systematic review OR meta-analysis)  -> 56 hits
recurrent pericarditis (meta-analysis[pt] OR systematic review[pt]) AND (colchicine OR treatment)  -> 37 hits

records.reason: CORP: double-blind placebo-controlled RCT of colchicine vs placebo in recurrent pericarditis (P/I/C/design all met).
CORP-2: double-blind placebo-controlled RCT of colchicine vs placebo in multiple recurrences of pericarditis.
ICAP: double-blind placebo-controlled RCT of colchicine vs placebo in pericarditis (acute setting; outcome is incessant/recurrent pericarditis) — within the prevention-of-recurrence scope.
COPE: open-label RCT with no placebo arm (colchicine vs aspirin, open-label) — fails the double-blind placebo-controlled design criterion.
COPPS: population is postpericardiotomy-syndrome prophylaxis in cardiac-surgery patients, not prevention of pericarditis recurrence — wrong population.
RESTORE: intervention is hydroxychloroquine and the comparator is colchicine (no placebo-controlled colchicine arm) — wrong intervention/comparison.
Anakinra vs prednisone in children — no colchicine-vs-placebo comparison — wrong intervention/comparison.
Norrid 2014: narrative review, not a randomized controlled trial.

COLCOT: colchicine vs placebo but in post-myocardial-infarction coronary disease — a primary trial of a DIFFERENT topic in this set (negative control). Correctly rejected despite same drug + double-blind design.

screening.positive_control: Search recovered the canonical double-blind colchicine-vs-placebo pericarditis RCTs (CORP, CORP-2, ICAP) that a colchicine-pericarditis meta-analysis includes; the open-label COPE was also recovered and excluded by the design rule.
screening.negative_control: COLCOT (PMID 31733140) — colchicine, double-blind, placebo-controlled, but post-MI coronary disease — was recovered by the search and correctly EXCLUDED (X5) as belonging to a different topic. Same drug + same design, different population: the screen rejects it.

outcomes.name: Recurrent pericarditis
outcomes.timepoint: longest reported recurrence follow-up (>=18 months for CORP/CORP-2)
outcomes.method: Random-effects inverse-variance on log(RR); Paule-Mandel tau^2; HKSJ 95% CI on t_{k-1} (variance floor max(1,Q/(k-1))); prediction interval mu +/- t_{k-1}*sqrt(tau2+se^2). Validated vs metafor 5.0.1.

trials.label: CORP
trials.source: Ann Intern Med 2011 abstract: recurrence 24% vs 55%; reported relative risk reduction 0.56 (95% CI 0.27-0.73) -> RR 0.44 (0.27-0.73). CT.gov has no results section; arm-level integer counts not stated in the abstract, so the reported effect+CI is used.

trials.label: CORP-2
trials.source: Lancet 2014 abstract: recurrent pericarditis 26/120 (21.6%) colchicine vs 51/120 (42.5%) placebo.

trials.label: ICAP
trials.source: N Engl J Med 2013 abstract: incessant or recurrent pericarditis 20/120 (16.7%) colchicine vs 45/120 (37.5%) placebo.

result.pi_note: tau^2 estimated as 0, so the prediction interval coincides with the confidence interval (no between-study heterogeneity detected).

outcomes.name: Gastrointestinal adverse events
outcomes.method: Random-effects inverse-variance on log(RR); Paule-Mandel tau^2; HKSJ 95% CI on t_{k-1} (variance floor max(1,Q/(k-1))); prediction interval mu +/- t_{k-1}*sqrt(tau2+se^2). Validated vs metafor 5.0.1.

declared_absent_trials.label: CORP
declared_absent_trials.reason: abstract states similar rates of side effects between groups; arm-level counts not given.

declared_absent_trials.label: ICAP
declared_absent_trials.reason: abstract states overall adverse effects similar and no serious adverse events; arm-level counts not given.

outcomes.name: Treatment discontinuation (drug withdrawal)
outcomes.method: Random-effects inverse-variance on log(RR); Paule-Mandel tau^2; HKSJ 95% CI on t_{k-1} (variance floor max(1,Q/(k-1))); prediction interval mu +/- t_{k-1}*sqrt(tau2+se^2). Validated vs metafor 5.0.1.

result.reason: All three included trials report study-drug discontinuation as similar between arms without extractable arm-level counts (CORP: 'similar drug withdrawal'; CORP-2: 'discontinuation in much the same proportions'; ICAP: 'rates of study-drug discontinuation similar').

comparator.name: Imazio et al., Efficacy and safety of colchicine for pericarditis prevention: systematic review and meta-analysis

only_theirs: open-label and older trials not in our double-blind-only scope; identities not enumerated in this build
overlap.note: CORP-2 (2014) and ICAP (2013) post-date the 2012 comparator and cannot be in it (only-ours, verifiable by date). CORP (2011) is date-eligible for the comparator. Our review restricts to double-blind placebo-controlled RCTs, so open-label trials the comparator pooled are only-theirs. Exact shared count is not asserted because the comparator's trial table was not extracted in this build.
